requirements.quote: The failure scenario above no longer reproduces at `bin/lean/heavy.mjs:310`, covered by a regression test that fails on the current staging head.
No behaviour change for lanes or repos the finding does not describe.

deliverables.change: guardChain(name, cmd, env, read=head): on a repeated name:cmd, only apply the next-PATH-match / shim_loop logic when isPassThroughWrapper(read(cmd), name); for a non-wrapper real binary return {cmd, env} unchanged without appending a chain entry (so nesting depth is not capped). Update the doc comments.

Regression test: runWrapped with PATH=/shim:/home/u/.nvm/bin, env FORGE_HEAVY_CHAIN=npm:<real> and FORGE_HEAVY_HELD=1, injected run: spawns the real npm (not 126), also at depth >= SHIM_LOOP_MAX of repeated real entries. Keep the existing wrapper-loop assertions passing (give the wrapper cases a wrapper-text read injection or real wrapper file).

preserve.what: Wrapper re-entry cutoff from #4680: a pass-through wrapper resolving back to the shim still gets the next PATH match or env.shim_loop (bin/lean/heavy.mjs guardChain, heavy.test.mjs:262-273)
runWrapped's FORGE_HEAVY_HELD / DISABLED / llm pass-through and the 126 exit on a real loop (bin/lean/heavy.mjs:331-334)

decisions.choice: Distinguish wrapper loops from legit nesting via the existing isPassThroughWrapper on the resolved cmd, rather than a new env marker
decisions.justification: heavy.mjs:256 already detects wrappers for #4680, deterministic and no new state; a wrapper loop and nested real call are otherwise indistinguishable by chain
